summary: Academy courses feature tested end-to-end. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases pass (builder validation 422s, role gating 403, draft->pending->reject(note)->approve->unpublish, paid outline stripping, done 403 without purchase, razorpay order for course:<id> reaches provider step (503), free/invalid course 400, sop-bundle regression, simulated purchase unlocks, quiz/lab/scenario server-side verification 400 then 200, 100% -> certificate SOCP-C-*, idempotent cert, public cert endpoint hides user_id). Frontend: instructor CourseBuilder (all 7 item types, ref picker auto-fills title, video-without-link shows 422 toast, save=draft, submit=pending), admin Courses tab (reject prompt -> review note shown in instructor editor, approve, unpublish, publish from editor), student /app/courses list cards (level, modules/items, Free/₹499/Owned), paid detail with locks + buy box (Razorpay disabled + 'Payments open soon'), owned flow (YouTube embed, SOP/SIEM open links, mark done, progress %, certificate link and certificate page with print). activate() code path for course:<id> inserts purchase; SOP/ebook branch unchanged. Two logic bugs found (see action items).

critical.issue: Instructor can edit a PUBLISHED course (title, price, modules) and the changes go live immediately with no admin re-review; status stays 'published'. Verified: instructor changed title and price 0->999 on a live course; students immediately saw it and a student who had already completed it lost access (owned:false) while still holding the certificate. This bypasses the 'admin approves before publish' requirement.

minor.issue: percent = len(done)/total uses all stored progress item_ids, including items later removed from the course. Verified percent=150 after the instructor removed an item. Fix: intersect done_set with the current item ids (and return only valid ids in 'done').
Any instructor gets every paid course for free (role check), not just their own. Probably intended for previews, but confirm it is.
Only published courses are returned, so instructors and admins can't preview a draft or pending course as a student would see it.

integration_issues.flow: Admin editor Publish -> back to list
integration_issues.issue: The list briefly shows the old status (DRAFT) until load() resolves, because CourseBuilder re-renders the old list state. Cosmetic only; the DB is correct.

issues: The nav item is labelled 'My Courses' (nav-my-courses), but it now lists the whole academy catalog; the request said 'Courses'.
If the description is empty, the 'About this course' box is a large empty panel. Hide it or show a fallback.
Button copy uses T.toLowerCase(), which gives 'Open siem simulator' / 'Open kali lab'. Keep the acronym casing.
No link back to the course or to the course list.

action_items: routes_academy.update: when a non-admin edits a published course, either set status back to 'pending' (keeping the live version until approved) or block edits until an admin unpublishes. At minimum, block price changes on published courses for non-admins.
routes_academy: compute percent/done from done_set & {current item ids} so progress can't go over 100%.
Optional: rename the sidebar label to 'Courses'; hide the empty description box; fix acronym casing in the 'Open ...' button; add a back link on the certificate page.
critical_code_review_comments: update() has no status transition, so post-publish edits skip review (see the critical issue).
Price changes on a published course aren't guarded. A free course turning paid takes access away from existing learners, including ones with certificates.
Item ids from the frontend aren't checked for uniqueness across modules. Duplicate ids would break progress tracking.
verify() for a lab passes silently if the lab id no longer exists.
get_cert is public (fine for verification) and correctly hides user_id.

success_rate.backend: 100% (17/17 tests); 1 high-severity logic gap and 1 minor bug found by manual probe
success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested flows work; minor design notes only

seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ courses, a TEST_ registered user, and a simulated purchase for the student on the TEST Paid Course. All were cleaned up: both courses were deleted via DELETE /api/academy/manage/{id} (including the original 'TEST Paid Course' 4a458bd451b4, as requested), along with their academy_progress, academy_certs and purchases rows. academy_courses is now empty.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_academy_courses.py -n 0 (it MUST use -n 0, because the tests share module state and xdist loadscope splits the classes). The test creates and cleans up its own courses and user, and simulates purchases and quiz/lab/scenario completion through mongo. UI note: after a student logs in, a level-up/rank-up overlay ([data-testid$='-reveal']) blocks clicks; dismiss it with the 'Continue' button. The admin reject flow uses window.prompt, so register an async dialog handler. Retest: an instructor edit of a published course should no longer go live without review, and percent should be capped at 100 after items are removed.
